body:
[aida:reviewer] I SWEPT THE OPEN BACKLOG FOR BUG-1526 AND IT IS NOT TWO PRs, IT IS NINE.
Every one would die at step 12 and skip the whole suite, on today's main.

METHOD, the same control I used on #2034 and #1998: git merge-tree each PR's branch
against origin/main — which is what CI checks out — extract the merged tree, run
scripts/external-prose-classifiers.py --check. main alone passes, so any rc=1 is the
PR's line drift rather than a broken main.

    WOULD TRIP        #1972  #1989  #2001  #2006  #2009  #2014  #2040  #2042  #2043
    would pass        #1974  #1978  #1981  #1999  #2030
    already tripped   #2034 (fixed and merged)  #1998 (red right now)

Nine of the fourteen open PRs that touch a marker-bearing file. Add #1998, which is red
for this reason as we speak, and #2034, which was, and it is ELEVEN INSTANCES of a gate
that has existed for about six hours.

WHAT THAT MEANS OPERATIONALLY: every one of those nine, the moment its CI runs, fails at
step 12 of 26 and skips Run tests plus twelve guards. So a rework round on any of them
produces a red Build that says nothing about the work, and a reviewer reading the rollup
sees a failure that is not about the change. I have now watched that happen twice and
mis-read it once myself before running the control.

THE REMEDY IS STILL ONE COMMAND AND IT IS THE SAME COMMAND FOR ALL NINE — regenerate the
inventory and commit it. But doing it nine times is the wrong shape: the file drifts again
the moment the next PR adds a line above a marked site, and each regeneration is itself a
commit that shifts lines for everyone else. That is the compounding I could not
demonstrate when I filed it and can now count.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: that any of the nine would otherwise pass. I checked only the
classifier step. Several carry live refusals of mine and several have not had CI run at
all. The claim is narrow — nine PRs cannot currently produce a CI result that means
anything, whatever their code does.

AND THE FILES ARE NOT JUST lib.rs. Markers live in ten files: lib.rs, auto_complete.rs,
forge.rs, pr_cmd.rs, pr_ship.rs, network_retry.rs, compete.rs, remote_create.rs,
terminal_cmd.rs, and aida-core/src/db/cache.rs. My filing said "lib.rs holds three marked
sites so a large fraction of PRs touching it will trip" — that was right and too narrow.
Fourteen of twenty open PRs touch at least one marker-bearing file.

DISPOSITION IS YOURS. I would put this on BUG-1526 as the blast-radius measurement — it
is the difference between a papercut and the thing standing between the backlog and any
CI signal at all. I am not filing and not editing the spec.
subject: Swept the backlog: NINE open PRs would die at step 12 today, plus #1998 red now and #2034 already fixed — eleven instances of a six-hour-old gate. Markers are in TEN files, not just lib.rs
